question: At which temperature is the density of water maximum?
solution:
The correct answer is __**277K**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The density of water is at its maximum at **4 degrees Celsius (39.2 degrees Fahrenheit or 277 Kelvin)**.
 
• When water freezes at **0°C (273.15 K)**, its density is lower than in any liquid state.
 
• At **4°C (39.2°F)** The density of pure water is at its **maximum**, approximately **1 g/cm³ (or 1000 kg/m³)**.
 
• The **boiling point **of** **water is **100°C (212°F)** and The **freezing point** of pure water is** 0°C (32°F)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
